episode_context.learner_goal: Understand how to solve and read Two Sum in Python without spending most of the effort decoding an author's coding style.

external_representation.loop_style: index-first range(len(...)) outer loop with indexed value access
external_representation.relevant_feature: the learner must translate index -> collection lookup -> value while also reasoning about the algorithm

learner_proposed_representation.loop_style: enumerate(...) with explicit index and value
learner_proposed_representation.relevant_feature: index and value are exposed directly

self_reported.text: The learner reported that decoding how another author wrote a solution can displace attention from solving the underlying problem.
The learner reported that the explicit index-and-value representation was less confusing than the index-first form used in the external solution.
The learner identified this episode as a reason an AI-mediated intermediate representation in Study OS could be valuable.

observed.text: Before being given the optimized implementation, the learner independently proposed using Python enumerate to expose both index and value.
The interaction then concentrated on why the authored solution used range(len(...)), whether enumerate was available in the selected Python runtime, and why the author did not use it.
The tutor rewrote the outer iteration into an explicit index-and-value form, removing the repeated mental translation from index to value access.
After the rewrite and discussion, the learner explicitly articulated the bottleneck as decoding somebody else's representation rather than focusing on the problem-solving idea.

derived.text: A candidate failure signature is representation translation overhead: the learner may understand or generate a clearer equivalent representation while incurring avoidable working-memory cost when reading an externally authored form.

Do not automatically classify this episode as a Python syntax deficit. The learner demonstrated familiarity with enumerate and independently suggested it; the observed friction centered on the external representation.

Test normalizing an unfamiliar external solution into a learner-comprehensible intermediate representation first, then later expose alternate author representations after the algorithmic invariant is stable.

intervention.to: explicit index-and-value iteration plus plain-language algorithmic invariant

claims_supported: This canonical Study OS episode provides direct subject-level evidence that externally authored code representation can itself become a learning bottleneck.
The learner's independently proposed explicit index-and-value representation was used to reduce one translation step in the explanation.
The episode supports testing representation normalization as an adaptive intervention for this learner.
not_yet_claimed: The episode does not establish durable Two Sum mastery.
The episode does not establish that enumerate is universally better for all learners or all problems.
The episode does not establish causal learning improvement from intermediate representation beyond the immediate interaction.
The episode does not yet contain an unaided reconstruction result, changed-surface transfer result, or delayed retention result.

follow_up_measurements.reason_hidden: Avoid contaminating a future transfer assessment by publishing the exact prompt before the learner attempts it.
